title: Typestate, Tokens, and RAII
goal: Enforce valid state transitions and resource cleanup using Rust ownership.

sections.text: In object-oriented programming, state machines rely on runtime checks and boolean flags. Rust models states as distinct types to catch invalid transitions at compile time.

sections.caption: unlock takes self by value and returns a new Door state.

sections.text: Taking `self` by value moves the locked door out of scope. You cannot call `unlock` twice because the borrow checker rejects using a moved value with error `E0382`.
You can also enforce permission by hiding private fields inside a module. Code outside the module cannot construct the type directly and must call your authorized constructor.

sections.caption: The private field prevents external instantiation.

sections.text: Finally, the `Drop` trait runs cleanup code automatically when a value leaves scope. This pattern is called Resource Acquisition Is Initialization or RAII.

explanation: Enforce valid state transitions and resource cleanup using Rust ownership.
